issues.description: The template StockIngredient class defines a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but the rest of the template (Stock.java) calls getQuantity(). The problem statement also asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" and the solution uses getQuantity(). This name mismatch is a structural inconsistency that will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the expected getter name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename retrieveQuantity() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java to getQuantity() (or add a public getQuantity() that delegates to retrieveQuantity()) so that it matches the getter naming required by the problem statement and the calls in Stock.java. Ensure all private fields have public getters with the expected getX() names as shown in the solution.

issues.description: The template defines a getter named retrieveQuantity() for StockIngredient, while the rest of the code and the solution expect the conventional getQuantity() name (used in Stock.add/take and in example Main). The problem statement also instructs to "add getters for all the private fields," which implies standard getter names. This naming mismatch will confuse students and cause compile/runtime mapping issues because code calls getQuantity() but the template provides retrieveQuantity().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java (or add a getQuantity() wrapper that calls retrieveQuantity()). This aligns the template with the problem statement conventions and with usages in Stock and Main, and matches the solution implementation.
